overview.summary: An array is a contiguous block of memory used to store a collection of items of the same type.
learningObjectives: Understand how contiguous memory allows O(1) index access.
Recognize the cost of shifting elements during insertions and deletions.
overview.interviewRelevance: Arrays are the most fundamental data structure. Almost every interview question relies on them.

paragraphs: Imagine a row of identical parking spaces. Every space has a number, and they are placed right next to each other.
If you know the number of a specific parking space, you can drive straight to it without checking the others.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: Because the spaces are contiguous, jumping to any specific slot is instant.

definition.technicalDefinition: An array is a data structure that stores elements in contiguous memory locations, allowing O(1) random access via an index.

vocabulary.definition: The numerical position of an element in the array (usually starting at 0).
Memory slots that are physically next to each other.
The ability to access any element instantly in O(1) time.

keyProperties: Fixed size in memory (in static languages).
O(1) time complexity to read or write a specific index.
O(n) time complexity to insert or delete elements (due to shifting).

metaphor: A set of post office boxes all in a single row.
mentalModel.clickSentence: Math makes it fast: Address = StartAddress + (Index * ItemSize).

memoryDescription: Arrays ask the operating system for one solid block of memory.
This guarantees that element [3] is physically adjacent to element [2].

steps.explanation: Search for 30. An array lets us read any index directly, so we simply walk left to right.
Read arr[0] in O(1) — the address is start + 0 × size. Value is 10.
Read arr[1] in O(1) — the address is start + 1 × size. Value is 20.
Read arr[2] in O(1) — the address is start + 2 × size. Value is 30.

operations.name: Access
operations.description: Read an element directly by its index.
operations.visualNote: The memory slot is accessed instantly.

operations.name: Search
operations.description: Iterate through the array to find a specific value.
operations.visualNote: Highlights each cell sequentially until the target is found.

patternTemplate.whenToUse: Use Arrays when you need fast random access and size is known or doesn't change frequently.
patternTemplate.spaceComplexity: O(n) memory to store n items.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You need to store a list of daily temperatures and frequently check the temperature on specific days by index.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: Arrays provide O(1) random access, making them perfect for looking up items by a known index.

examples.title: Contains Duplicate
examples.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array.
steps: Store seen values in a Hash Set.
If a value is already in the set, we found a duplicate.
examples.rationale: We traverse the array once while utilizing auxiliary space to track elements.

conceptQuiz.question: Why is array access O(1)?
options: Elements are contiguous, so memory addresses are calculated with simple math.
The computer searches all elements instantly.
Arrays are stored in the CPU cache.
Arrays are mapped to hash values.
conceptQuiz.explanation: The memory address of any index is found by adding (Index * Size) to the starting address.

conceptQuiz.question: What is the primary drawback of a static array?
options: Fixed size means you must guess capacity up front.
Accessing the middle element is slow.
conceptQuiz.explanation: Static arrays cannot grow. If you run out of space, you must create a new, larger array.

practice.title: Two Sum
practice.keyInsight: Iterate the array while storing complements in a hash map.

practice.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
practice.keyInsight: Track the lowest minimum price as you iterate.
